Controls: both arms use the same unmodified configs/150M.json (880/16, rotary), optimizer, schedule, data order, 2B stop and a single GPU SKU. The known asymmetries (tokenizer-plus-head package, 1.2% parameter difference) are carried and disclosed. Data: the apparatus and data are pinned by hash. Metric: the metric is the same density NLL as at 60M, on all 172,032 held-out targets, equal-weighted by source; in-corpus NLL is diagnostic only. Safeguards: a model-free floor diagnostic runs before any NLL, and S1–S5 can only remove a verdict. The invalidation list is comprehensive. Held-out reuse from the 60M selection is unavoidable under the brief's fixed evaluation set. It is disclosed, no 150M selection is permitted, and S5 bounds it under an assumption stated as such. I judge the comparison defensible with that disclosure.

Execution plan: six runs from scratch, with exact v2 CLI commands and pre-flight tests. Card: an H100 80GB, the same SKU as all 12 60M runs. Throughput: estimated from the v1 150M benchmark scaled by 60M ratios (A ~3.6 h, B ~3.3 h, 20.8 GPU-h). The arithmetic checks, and the plan states that the brief's ~2 h/run figure is exceeded. Budget: a spend gate with 1.25× headroom ($95.20) against the $200 cap includes other experiments' spend, and nothing starts if the gate fails or no GPU is available. A smaller card is allowed only after smoke runs. Failure handling: crashes and divergence are retained, nothing is resumed or replaced, and no run is simulated. The checkpoint-capture fix for the 60M sort bug is included. Limitations are enumerated: no 150M sweep, B's rate at the grid edge, held-out reuse, three seeds, one training source, whole-package effect, observations not FLOPs, estimated throughput. Minor execution notes (unrounded Δ reference, S4 fallback) are given in the review notes and are not blocking.

reviews.synopsis: All six 150M runs followed the approved plan: one H100 each, the carried rates, exactly 2B observations. Recomputed numbers match the run files and exhibit. The primary result is UNDETERMINED (mu[A] <= 0). The pre-registered sign-safe ordering gives QUANTILE-BETTER, and S1 and S5 hold. So C1 is contradicted as written and the 60M ordering holds at 150M. The paper edits are accurate.

findings.notes:
The six runs match the plan's allocation:
- A 3e-4 / B 1e-4, seeds 101/202/303, unmodified configs/150M.json (e7f765b2…8864), rotary positions.
- Exact planned commands with no forbidden flags; 2,000,000,000 observations and 244,160 steps; the final checkpoint scored and retained.
- All 172,032 held-out targets scored; one H100 80GB HBM3 SKU; consistent manifest, tokenizer, freeze and code hashes.
- Parameter counts equal the plan's expected values.

The diagnostic predates all training: produced at 12:04:25Z, artifact created at 12:05:19Z, first job start 12:12:32Z. It reproduces the reference exactly (T, E, bins, Δ, mask hash).

No invalidation condition fired. Deviations are listed and explained in the report: split sessions, the refused pre-provision launch, the A-202 capture retry, unconditional rescore kept out of the verdict, the CPU diagnostic environment, the spend gate not observed at lease time with final spend under the cap, and throughput. None changes rates, seeds, metric or rules.

I recomputed the per-run primaries from the source means, and mu, ranges, D, R, δ_A/δ_B, the ordering inequalities, S1 and both S5 shifts from the run files. All match verdict-analysis.json and the report table to the printed precision.

The exhibit's heldout_nll values, file hashes, band mu values and label match the artifacts. The report tabulates every run with per-source NLL, the in-corpus diagnostic, wall-clock, throughput and cost. It also discloses rework: the corrected first-start timestamp, the capture retry and the refused launch.

The report states the primary label first (UNDETERMINED, unevaluable because mu[A] <= 0) and does not treat the formal R as a result. It then applies the pre-registered secondary rule, QUANTILE-BETTER, which survives S1 and S5.

The C1 reading follows the plan's pre-registered mapping: patch did not improve at 150M, so C1 is contradicted as written. That is a negative finding stated plainly.

The C2 reading gives matching orderings, a gap ratio of 0.975 under the plan's proposed band, and the caveat that two sizes cannot separate closing from stabilizing and cannot extrapolate to 1.3B. It leaves judgement to the reflection.

The listed limitations are transferred LRs, B at the grid edge, unmeasured held-out reuse bounded only by S5's assumption, and the whole-package scope. The report also restates the fictional scope and the LOTSA-only measurement.

The Methods addition matches the plan and the run files: config and parameter counts, rates and their provenance, the S5 deltas, seeds and metric, the primary and secondary rules, the card, and about 155k/208k obs/s. It is written against revision 2 and leaves existing sections unchanged.

The Results addition quotes the per-seed NLLs, means, ranges, per-source seed means, D, the formal R, the ordering inequality, S1, the S5 agreement, the zero sub-floor targets, and the C1/C2 readings. All agree with the retained evidence and keep the scope disclaimer.

One minor imprecision is not blocking: "S2-S4 were not triggered (E empty)" folds together distinct reasons. S2 was untriggered because S1 passed.

reviews.synopsis: The plan is honest, well controlled and runnable, but it cannot answer its research question. C3 and the brief require evaluation at 4,096-step context, and the frozen apparatus only evaluates 256-observation windows. The plan itself pre-registers C3 at 4,096 as not tested under every outcome. Before a plan can pass, it needs either a 4,096-capable apparatus or an owner decision re-scoping C3.

findings.notes: The hypothesis is testable only in a form that differs from the one the experiment exists to test. The brief's research question and claim C3 (claim_049e1e1f27644766bfabe595070f82a2) are explicitly at 4,096-step context. The brief says 'THE EVALUATION SET IS THE WHOLE POINT. Evaluate at 4,096-step context ... and on nothing else.' I checked the plan's incompatibility finding against the accepted v2 README/CHANGES (art_7681f07020544efe917637112773a405). It confirms 256-observation windows (32 normalization + 224 scored), 255 quantile input positions, no context flag, and model.py/prepare.py unchanged from v1. So the disclosure is accurate. The consequence is that the plan's own pre-registration says 'C3 at 4,096-step context: NOT TESTED under every outcome.' A design whose every outcome leaves the claim untested cannot distinguish that claim from its alternatives. The substitute question at 256 is also a weak proxy, and the gap is not small. The main scientific difference between learned absolute and rotary positions is behaviour over long ranges and beyond the trained length. At a 256 window, both arms stay inside a range the absolute table was trained on, so the result gives little information about 4,096 in either direction. The plan admits this in its limitations. Reframing the Objective to '256-observation window' changes the research question rather than answering it. Required correction: either (a) an apparatus task delivers 4,096-observation held-out windows, a window-4,096 150M config and a matching absolute table, and a new plan re-estimates cost, which will be much higher; or (b) the owner explicitly re-scopes C3 and the brief to the 256 window, and a new plan cites that decision. The plan correctly flags this as an operator decision. The reviewer cannot make that decision on the owner's behalf by passing it.

For the comparison the plan actually proposes, the controls are strong. --position is the only varied flag. The config, tokenizer and calibration, schedule, data order, 2B budget (244,160 steps), evaluator and GPU class are identical across arms, and invalidation condition 4 checks this from run.json hashes. Seeds 101/202/303 are disjoint from sweep and default seeds. The plan correctly notes that the absolute table shifts RNG, so seed-matched differences are only descriptive. LR 0.0003 is shared in both arms with no 150M tuning. The asymmetry that it was tuned with rotary at 60M is disclosed and conservative for C3 support: it biases toward a gap, not toward equivalence. No selection happens on held-out data at 150M, so the 150M evaluation is disjoint from any 150M choice, in line with the 12:05Z waiver's instruction. The evaluation-set verification steps (a)-(d) tie each primary number to manifest['eval'] via code and manifest hashes and exact by-source keys and counts. The decision statistic uses |m_A| with an unevaluability floor of 0.10 nats, which fixes the 60M sign problem. Supports requires D<1% with overlapping ranges; anything else in 1–3% is undetermined. The data and metric match the claim's scope in every respect except context length, and that mismatch is assessed under criterion 1.

Execution at 256 is feasible and failure modes are handled well. The plan uses the measured 150M throughput (156k obs/s, about 3.6 h/run), not the brief's 2 h, and derives about 24 GPU-h / about $80. It gates launch on spend_status covering all six runs plus 10%, because the ~$116 remaining cap is shared with tokenizer-ab-150m-2 and a partial seed set invalidates the test. It also forbids running or simulating anything if GPUs or cap are unavailable, specifies relaunch-from-scratch disclosure because resume is not implemented, and guards against the 60M checkpoint-copy bug. The limitations list covers the 256-vs-4,096 context, rotary-only LR tuning, held-out-selected LR, three seeds, a single training source and LOTSA-only scope. I did not independently verify the spend figure ($84.08); the launch gate makes that safe. A replacement plan at 4,096 would need a fresh cost estimate, since attention cost rises sharply with context and may not fit the remaining cap.

reviews.synopsis: The 4,096-context design is scientifically sound, and its arithmetic checks out. But the plan says it cannot run. It depends on an apparatus task (A1–A7) that does not exist and is not linked. Its evaluator and loader are only specifications, the spend gate is probably not met, and owner decisions are still open. Approving it would send a design with no runnable apparatus into execution.

findings.notes: The design now tests C3 as stated. Both arms train and are evaluated at 4,096-step context, on 47 windows cut only from the frozen held-out arrays of the three named sources. Four outcomes are distinguished: supports, rotary better, absolute better and undetermined. D = 100·|m_R−m_A|/|m_A| uses a sign-safe denominator with an unevaluability floor of 0.10 nats. Supports needs D<1% with overlapping closed ranges, D>3% contradicts, and everything else is undetermined. This matches the brief's rule and fixes the 60M sign problem. The 256-window scores are labelled secondary and cannot override the primary result. No extrapolation claim is made, which is correct because both arms train at 4,096. This criterion is met at the level of design; that the design can be executed is assessed under criterion 3.

The arms differ only in --position. Config, tokenizer, schedule, data order, budget, evaluator and GPU class are shared. Invalidation condition 4 checks this from run.json, and conditions 1, 5 and 6 bar any other evaluation set or context and any execution without G1. The extra 3.6M-parameter absolute table (2.39%) is part of the method and is disclosed. The data change is identical in both arms: 5.1% of observations repeat, with a 3,072-observation overshoot. The plan's arithmetic re-checks exactly, and so do the held-out window counts and target counts. The held-out data is used only for evaluation, so no 150M selection touches it, as the 12:05Z waiver requires. The shared LR was tuned with rotary at 60M/256. That asymmetry biases away from supporting C3 and is disclosed. Caveats for the next version: (i) the plan departs from 'the 150M configuration exactly as delivered' and 'exactly 2B'. This is scientifically minimal and defensible, but it is an owner decision that the plan flags and does not yet cite. (ii) The evaluation-set verification steps (a)–(d) refer to evaluator outputs that do not exist yet, so they must be re-stated against the delivered A4 fields. (iii) Two points should be added as limitations: standardizing on 32 observations in a 4,096 window, and an LR selected at 256/32-window batches being applied at 4,096/2-window batches.

By the plan's own statement it cannot execute. First, G1 and G2 fail: workflow.status_and_next lists rates-from-60m as the only prerequisite, and no A1–A7 apparatus task exists or is linked. The loader, evaluator, config, freeze and launch command are specifications, not delivered code, and the command is only an 'expected form'. Second, G3 is probably unmet. The FLOP estimate of 30–37 GPU-h, about $97–$120, is sound and honestly corrects the brief's 12 GPU-h. Against $115.92 remaining, shared with tokenizer-ab-150m-2, the plan concedes the gate is probably not met without an owner decision. Third, A7 may make execution depend on resume support that does not exist. The failure-mode handling is good: no simulation, relaunch disclosure, checkpoint tokens_seen check, and a partial seed set invalidates the test. The limitations list is thorough. But a design approval should pin a plan that can run on accepted apparatus. The operator rule for v2 (a design that waits on an unaccepted apparatus is not submitted for review) applies directly. Required before resubmission: an accepted and linked A1–A7 task; the plan updated to its artifact ids, hashes, real commands and output fields; costs re-estimated from the A6 measurement; and recorded owner decisions on the config and budget deviation and on the spend cap or ordering.

reviews.synopsis: The 4,096-context design is sound and now lists both limitations suggested last time. But it cannot run: no accepted A1–A7 apparatus task exists or is linked, and the loader, evaluator and launch command are unwritten. The spend gate fails and three owner decisions are unrecorded, so the plan cannot be approved yet.

findings.notes:
The design tests C3 as stated. Both arms train and are evaluated at 4,096-step context, on 47 windows cut only from the frozen held-out arrays of australian_electricity_demand, pedestrian_counts and traffic_hourly.

Five outcomes are distinguished: supports, contradicted with rotary lower, contradicted with absolute lower, undetermined, and unevaluable. The statistic D = 100·|m_R−m_A|/|m_A| uses a sign-safe denominator, with an unevaluability floor of |m_A| < 0.10 nats. The 1%/3% bands with an overlapping-range condition match the brief, and D < 1% with disjoint ranges is correctly reported as undetermined.

The secondary 256-window scores, position buckets and in-corpus values are labelled descriptive and cannot override the verdict. This is met at the level of design; whether it can execute is judged under criterion 3.

The arms differ only in --position. Config, tokenizer, schedule, data order, budget, evaluator and GPU class are shared, and invalidation condition 4 checks this from run.json. The absolute arm's extra 3,604,480 parameters (+2.394%) are intrinsic to the method and disclosed.

The data changes apply identically to both arms: 5.1% of observations repeat, and the budget overshoots 2B by 3,072. Held-out data is used only for final evaluation, so selection and evaluation are disjoint at 150M, as the 12:05Z waiver requires. The rotary-tuned LR inherited from 60M/256 is an asymmetry that biases against supporting C3; it is disclosed, and so is its untested transfer to 4,096 context with 2-window batches. The late-position standardization limitation is now included.

Open caveats for the next version:
- The config and budget deviations still need a recorded owner decision.
- Verification steps (a)–(d) name evaluator fields that do not exist yet, so they must be re-stated against the delivered A4 output.

The plan itself states that it cannot execute, and the live checks confirm it.

- G1/G2 not met: workflow.status_and_next lists rates-from-60m as the only prerequisite, and no A1–A7 task is linked. The v2 apparatus has no context flag, a 256-row absolute table, a budget that must divide by 256, and no checkpoint resume. The loader, evaluator, config, freeze and command therefore exist only as specifications.
- G3 not met: the plan's own figures give about $194 committed against the $200 cap once tokenizer-ab-150m-2's live runs finish, which leaves under $15 against an estimated $97–$120.
- A7: at the estimated 4.6–5.8 h per run plus setup, some runs may exceed the 6 h lease without resume support, which does not exist.
- No owner decision is recorded at contextRevision 9.

The failure-mode handling is good: no simulation, disclosed relaunches, a tokens_seen check before the final checkpoint, and a partial seed set is never launched. The limitations list is thorough and the compute re-costing is honest.

None of that makes this pinned plan executable. Required before resubmission: an accepted and linked A1–A7 task (or an owner re-scope of C3 to 256), the plan updated to that task's artifact ids and hashes, real commands and output fields, compute re-costed from measured A6 throughput with A7 resume evidence if needed, and recorded owner decisions on the deviations and the spend cap or ordering.

reviews.synopsis: The deterministic manifest evaluation is well designed, but the plan pins obsolete v1 configurations and launch instructions. Accepted v2 changes more than LR/seed support. Update the apparatus pins and installation inventory before execution; retain the unchanged corpus pins and existing controls.

findings.notes: Objective & hypothesis and Evaluation define a falsifiable repository-fidelity/metadata test: valid shard digests and sizes, exactly 2,000,000,000 training observations, and zero held-out source overlap. Named assertion failures and separate provenance/environment invalidation distinguish success from alternatives. Scope correctly excludes model quality and full-array truth; no statistical baseline or GPU experiment is needed for this deterministic question.

The valid/mutated fixtures, independent delivery count, repository-byte identity checks and shard/provenance-level source separation are defensible controls, with identity and semantic tests separated to avoid masking defects. However, Pinned apparatus and data chooses art_1506682239c9429db2ad48cf91072c35 and v1 config/README/freeze hashes as the reference despite the assignment requiring accepted v2 for every experiment. Passing those checks could certify the unchanged manifest while installing obsolete configurations, calibration and launch instructions. Pin v2 archive and relevant delivery evidence, update imported member identities and SOURCES.json requirements, and quote the v2 README launch command. Keep the unchanged manifest/count/held-out references and current controls.

CPU-only verification of a roughly 54 MB manifest, single-object acquisition, standard-library checks, code.commit checkpoints and final workspace capture are technically feasible. Missing inputs, symlink/path escape, malformed metadata, provenance mismatch, implementation rework and commit self-reference are addressed. Nevertheless the exact execution plan instructs preflight to stop for a revised design if an accepted successor changes the apparatus; accepted v2 is already present in the assignment and demonstrably changes required files. Thus this pinned plan cannot reach delivery under its own guard. Resolve the known release mismatch during planning, preserve the no-GPU/no-shard-download boundary, and retain the guard for genuinely subsequent changes.

reviews.synopsis: The pinned v2 plan can answer the repository-fidelity question. It corrects the obsolete apparatus selection and combines independent release pins, manifest invariants and mutation controls with feasible offline evaluation. All three design criteria are met; implementation results remain to be established.

findings.notes: Objective & hypothesis and Evaluation define a falsifiable test of committed repository fidelity and manifest metadata: valid digest/size on every shard, exactly 2,000,000,000 training observations, and no held-out training source overlap, together with complete v2 identity. The exact primary command, named diagnostics, nonzero failure exits, separate invalidation conditions and explicit PASS rule distinguish a correct installation from semantic failure, provenance mismatch and invalid evaluation. Claims are appropriately limited to metadata consistency and repository fidelity, excluding array truth and model or industrial generalization.

The accepted v2 release is an appropriate deterministic reference. Artifact and manifest pins, exact training/evaluation counts, fixed held-out names, complete member inventory and retained provenance prevent certification from self-consistent but changed candidate metadata. Source separation is checked at top-level, shard and provenance levels with agreement checks, and evaluation observations are excluded from the training total. Valid and single-defect fixtures exercise the same semantic function independently of hash rejection. Separate identity controls cover altered manifest, false artifact digest, v1 config substitution and missing/altered v2 calibration even when the manifest is unchanged. Source evidence confirms the v2 choice and quoted launch commands. The plan therefore resolves the prior baseline mismatch without weakening corpus controls; replication or statistical thresholds are unnecessary.

The execution is feasible as standard-library CPU verification of one roughly 54 MB manifest and small retained artifacts in the runner-provided private Git checkout. Acquisition is limited to Merv and project storage, with no GPU, shard downloads or launch execution; evaluation consumes repository files only. The plan addresses missing inputs, unsuitable checkout, unsafe archive paths and external symlinks, malformed types, digest mismatches, incomplete release inventory, later apparatus changes, preserved failed runs and committed fixes. code.commit checkpoints, clean-tree/Git-blob checks, explicit evaluated/reporting commits, rerun on the final reporting commit, results.json and final workspace capture provide a concrete evidence chain without commit self-reference. The known v2 preflight conflict is resolved. Actual acquisition, implementation and evaluation remain execution work, with limitations explicitly stated.

reviews.synopsis: The v2 installation, provenance checks, verifier and 14 controls are sound and honestly reported, but the pre-registered primary evaluation never ran: the full manifest was not acquired, so all three assertions are not_evaluated and the verifier exits 1. The plan is valid. Repair under it in a lease with sandboxes storage access by committing the manifest and rerunning.

findings.notes:
Execution followed the approved plan up to the manifest. At capture D:
- The six artifacts are retained under vendor/ and provenance/.
- The 45 v2 members are imported, with v1 kept only as a test fixture.
- SOURCES.json, INTEGRATION.md, the standard-library verifier and the committed controls are present.
- The C/D separation is present and the report states that the harness is unchanged between them.

The core pre-registered step did not happen. The full manifest was never acquired or committed (harness/data/ is absent), so the primary command exits 1 and none of shard_metadata, observation_total or held_out_disjoint was evaluated. The held-out file had to be derived from archive members instead of the manifest's eval_source_ids.

The deviations are explained honestly: no storage tool in the lease, local git instead of code.commit, and Python 3.11. The plan itself classifies a missing manifest as blocking. The fix is to rerun under the same plan with storage access, commit the manifest and run the evaluation.

The committed results/harness-in-repo/results.json matches art_c8798cc7 field for field: BLOCKED, null shard_count and observation_total, three not_evaluated assertions, provenance with only the manifest failing, 6/45/24 matches, controls 14/14, exit 1 and Python 3.11.7.

verify_manifest.stdout confirms the single error "missing file: harness/data/manifest.json" and not_evaluated for all three assertions. controls.unittest.log shows 14 tests OK, with names matching the report's list of controls. The exhibit art_6223caa8 restates results.json and keeps the 60/2B/3/196,608 reference values under a key marked as not measured.

The report discloses its rework: a draft commit-hash typo, four superseded report uploads, and the derivation of the held-out file. Nothing material appears to be hidden.

The one-sentence Conclusion says the harness is installed and its provenance verified in 25e8f15, but that the test is blocked (no valid test of H1): the manifest was not acquired, the verifier exits 1 and no assertion was evaluated. That follows exactly from the evidence and claims no pass or fail of H1.

The Limitations section correctly limits even a completed run to metadata consistency and repository fidelity, not array contents or model performance, and describes sources as LOTSA sub-datasets. No paper changes are proposed, which is appropriate because no finding was produced. The report also lists the concrete steps that would complete the experiment.

reviews.synopsis: The repair run did what the approved plan required. The real manifest bytes are now committed. On clean commit 41bf99e the verifier exits 0 and all three assertions pass: 60 shards, 2B training observations and no held-out overlap. Provenance and all 14 controls pass. The results, exhibit, report and proposed Methods text agree with the checkout, and the earlier BLOCKED run is kept and disclosed.

findings.notes:
The repair followed the approved plan and the previous review's repair list:
- It fetched the single object obj_9z92tagytddvhzqp and committed its real bytes at harness/data/manifest.json. The file is present in the checkout and is not an LFS pointer.
- It re-derived held_out_sources.json from eval_source_ids, as plan step 4 requires.
- It regenerated SOURCES.json.
- It evaluated the clean commit C2 and reported in D2, whose harness is unchanged per the report.
- It reran on D2.
- It kept the earlier BLOCKED outputs.

The verifier pins the plan's values and cross-checks eval_source_ids. The report explains the deviations: local git instead of code.commit, Python 3.11, two evaluation rounds, and repository size.

The numbers agree across all sources. The committed stdout shows 60 training shards, 2,000,000,000 training observations, 3 evaluation shards, 196,608 evaluation observations, overlap [] and train_sources [era5_1989]. It also shows the manifest sha256 a23b9537…edaf. The committed results.json and art_96b314c0 report the same values, and the exhibit art_7e7f3d96 restates them exactly. The unittest log shows 14/14 OK. The report discloses the earlier BLOCKED round and the files that changed in C2.

The one-sentence PASS conclusion follows from the pre-registered rule. All three assertions hold, the verifier exits 0, provenance passes, the controls pass and no INVALID condition was triggered. The report states its limits: metadata and repository fidelity only, no shard array contents, and no model performance claim. It also notes that training uses a single source.

The proposed Methods section apparatus-and-corpus (against revision 0) is supported by the evidence:
- The v2 archive ID and hash, commit 41bf99e and the manifest object, hash and size match the plan pins and results.
- The configs (640/12 and 880/16, patch 16, seed 1729, learning rate 3e-4) and the tokenizer calibration match the plan.
- 60 shards, 2B observations from era5_1989, the three held-out sources with 196,608 evaluation observations, and the verifier's scope all match the stdout and results.json.

It correctly limits the check to metadata and repository fidelity.

limits: Trajectories and verdicts are asserted after the fact; no verdict text reaches any worker.
A stage carrying a planted defect is launched by this harness, not the runner: the runner builds its child stdin from the frozen assignment and has no per-assignment prompt hook.
The production feed has no voices: each brief post is written by the source credential with its named role as a body prefix.
Reflection, consolidation and post-wave claim updates are outside this harness slice.
